Software Engineering Lab 2: Agile Backlog Creation & Sprint Simulation in Jira

Telemedicine Slot Booking & Prescription Portal (Problem Statement #11, Healthcare & Telemedicine) Jira project: Telemedicine Slot Booking Portal (TSB), a company-managed Scrum project.

1. Scope and Source Requirements

This lab converts the Lab 1 requirements for the Telemedicine Slot Booking & Prescription Portal into an Agile backlog and runs it through two sprints in Jira.

Lab 1 Req Description Priority Backlog item
FR-001 Physicians author and digitally sign structured prescriptions compiled into PDF records High TSB-12
FR-002 Patients view slots by physician specialty and book a video consultation slot High TSB-4, TSB-5, TSB-6, TSB-7
FR-003 Generate and securely deliver a unique tele-consultation room link per appointment High TSB-8, TSB-9, TSB-10
FR-004 Physician accesses the patient record and submits a prescription after the consultation High TSB-11, TSB-12
FR-005 Patients download digitally signed prescription records Medium TSB-13
NFR-001 Session metadata and clinical notes encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3) and at rest (AES-256) High TSB-9
NFR-002 Role-based access control over records, rooms and prescriptions High TSB-10, TSB-11

2. Epics

Key Epic Covers Requirements
TSB-1 Appointment Booking A patient finds a physician by specialty, books an open video consultation slot, and can move that booking if plans change. FR-002
TSB-2 Secure Consultation Room Every confirmed appointment gets a unique room link, delivered to both participants and closed to everyone else. FR-003, NFR-001, NFR-002
TSB-3 Prescription Lifecycle After the consultation the physician records it and issues a signed prescription the patient can download. FR-001, FR-004, FR-005, NFR-002

3. User Stories, Story Points and Priority

Key Epic User Story Priority Points Traces to
TSB-4 TSB-1 Browse specialties and available slots — As a patient, I want to browse physicians by specialty and see the consultation slots they have open, so that I can find an appointment that fits my schedule. High 3 FR-002
TSB-5 TSB-1 Book a video consultation slot — As a patient, I want to select an open slot and confirm the booking, so that my consultation is reserved with a specific physician and time. High 5 FR-002
TSB-6 TSB-1 Prevent double-booking of a slot — As a patient, I want the system to re-check availability at the moment I confirm and refuse a slot someone else has taken, so that two patients are never booked into the same consultation. High 5 FR-002
TSB-8 TSB-2 Generate a unique consultation room link — As a patient, I want a unique tele-consultation room to be created once my booking is confirmed, so that there is a private place for the consultation to happen. High 5 FR-003
TSB-9 TSB-2 Deliver the room link to both participants — As an attending physician, I want the room link sent securely to me and to the patient, so that neither of us has to chase the other for it. High 3 FR-003, NFR-001
TSB-10 TSB-2 Restrict room access to booked participants — As a patient, I want the consultation room to admit only the booked patient and the assigned physician, so that nobody else can join a private medical consultation. High 8 FR-003, NFR-002
TSB-11 TSB-3 Access the patient consultation record — As an attending physician, I want to open the record of the patient I am consulting with, so that I can see their history before I prescribe anything. High 5 FR-004, NFR-002
TSB-12 TSB-3 Author and digitally sign a prescription — As an attending physician, I want to write a structured prescription and sign it with my verified credentials, so that the prescription is legally attributable to me. High 8 FR-001, FR-004
TSB-7 TSB-1 Reschedule a booked consultation — As a patient, I want to move a confirmed consultation to a different open slot, so that I do not have to cancel and rebook when my plans change. Medium 3 FR-002
TSB-13 TSB-3 Download a signed prescription PDF — As a patient, I want to download the signed prescription for a completed consultation, so that I have a verifiable record I can take to a pharmacy. Medium 3 FR-005

Total: 48 story points across 10 stories.

Estimating with planning poker

Story points measure relative effort, not hours. The Fibonacci scale is used because the gaps widen as the numbers grow, which stops a team arguing over a 6 against a 7 on work nobody understands well enough to separate. Each member reveals a card at the same time so nobody anchors on the loudest voice; where the cards disagree, the highest and lowest explain their reasoning and the round is re-run.

Two stories came out at 8. TSB-10 is large because access control has to hold against a real attempt to join another patient's room, and TSB-12 because a signature has to be verifiable by a third party.

Prioritising and ranking the backlog

Priority follows patient safety and privacy, not feature appeal. Unauthorised access to a consultation room or a clinical record is a privacy breach, so TSB-10 and TSB-11 sit at High alongside the core booking path.

The backlog was then reordered so that rank matches priority: all eight High stories above the two Medium ones, dependency order preserved inside the High band, since a room cannot be secured before it can be generated. Both sprints pull from the top of that list. One consequence is that rescheduling and the prescription download are conveniences, so both sit at Medium and neither has been started.

4. Sprint Execution

Two sprints, one week each. Both were simulated: stories were moved To Do → In Progress → Done within a single session, so the sprint duration is one week while the recorded activity is compressed into minutes. This shows up in the shape of the burndown chart.

Sprint 1

Goal: A patient can find a physician by specialty, book a video consultation slot, and have a room link reach both participants.

Key Story Points Outcome
TSB-4 Browse specialties and available slots 3 Done
TSB-5 Book a video consultation slot 5 Done
TSB-6 Prevent double-booking of a slot 5 Done
TSB-8 Generate a unique consultation room link 5 Done
TSB-9 Deliver the room link to both participants 3 Done

Committed 21. Delivered 21.

The goal was met in full. A patient can browse specialties, book a slot without any risk of double-booking, and both participants receive the consultation room link before the appointment. Nothing carried over.

Sprint 2

Goal: Lock the consultation room down to its two participants and let the physician record the consultation and issue a signed prescription.

Key Story Points Outcome
TSB-10 Restrict room access to booked participants 8 Done
TSB-11 Access the patient consultation record 5 Done
TSB-12 Author and digitally sign a prescription 8 Blocked — carried over

Committed 21. Delivered 13. TSB-12 was blocked, so no prescription can be signed and FR-001 is still not met.

Progress comments

Progress went into comments on the issues, not only into status changes, so the board carries the reasoning as well as the outcome. The comment that matters is on TSB-12, written once it was clear it would not finish:

"Not finishing this sprint. The editor is complete, but signing depends on a certificate from an external provider that the team does not control and did not request until after the sprint had started. The 8 covered the work; it did not cover the wait. Carrying over, and the dependency should have been raised at sprint planning."

Position after two sprints

Points Stories
Delivered 34 7
Remaining in backlog 14 3 (TSB-12, TSB-7, TSB-13)
Total 48 10

Velocity: 21, then 13.

5. Reflection

Did the estimations reflect the actual effort?

For nine of the ten stories, yes. The booking-path 3s and 5s behaved as estimated, and TSB-10 at 8 was correctly sized. TSB-12 is the interesting case, because the estimate was not wrong: eight points was a fair reading of the work, but the team did not control the signing certificate it depended on.

Story points measure effort, not waiting. An external dependency has to be cleared before the story is committed.

Was the backlog well-prioritised?

Largely. Priority followed safety and privacy, the backlog was ranked to match, and both sprints pulled from the top. The two privacy-critical stories, TSB-10 and TSB-11, are done, and the two untouched stories are both Medium conveniences.

The gap is subtler. TSB-12 is the story that makes FR-001 real, and it is the one still outstanding. Ranking by impact says what matters most; it says nothing about what is most likely to fail. A risk column beside priority would have surfaced the external dependency before the sprint started.

How did the simulated sprint align with the plan?

Sprint 1 aligned exactly: 21 committed, 21 delivered, goal met. Sprint 2 did not: 21 committed, 13 delivered, goal missed with the largest story blocked.

The second commitment was 21 because the first sprint had delivered 21, which felt like evidence. One clean sprint is a single data point, and 21 against 13 establishes no velocity yet.

What did the burndown chart show about capacity?

The event log is where the burndown is legible:

Event Burned Remaining
Sprint start, 3 stories added — 21
TSB-10 completed 8 13
TSB-11 completed 5 8
Sprint ended — 8 (TSB-12 blocked)

The line falls steeply and then stops flat at 8. That flat tail is the signal: work stopped moving entirely rather than slowing down.

The plotted curve is compressed, and the reason matters. The To Do → In Progress → Done moves were all made inside one session, so every event lands in the first minutes of a seven-day axis rather than spreading across it, and the remaining-work line drops almost vertically instead of stepping down beside the guideline. That is an artifact of the simulation, not a property of the plan.

In a real sprint that flat tail would be a warning sign, and here it was accurate: nothing the team did in the remaining time-box could have moved TSB-12.

What the team would take into the next sprint

  1. Clear external dependencies before committing the story. The TSB-12 certificate should have been requested in Sprint 1.
  2. Do not treat one clean sprint as a velocity. Sprint 1 delivering 21 made 21 look safe for Sprint 2, and the two together delivered 21 and 13.
  3. Finish TSB-12 first. FR-001 is the only High requirement still outstanding.
